subject: Aligning throughput & budget: target $/1M, token ranges, and continuous-batching expectations

Subject: Quick follow-up: volumes, $/1M target and batching assumptions

Hi Mark — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Helpful context. I promised to follow up with a concise list of the numbers we need to model cost and a suggested next-step cadence. Can you confirm the items below (even rough ranges are fine):

- Expected monthly token volume (range is OK; e.g., 50M–200M/month)
- Target unit economics (target $ / 1M tokens you want to land at)
- Monthly budget band or commit range you’re comfortable testing under a pilot
- Workload mix: % of traffic that is short chatty messages vs. long-generation (summaries/batch jobs) vs. embeddings
- Concurrency profile: baseline concurrent requests, expected business-hour peaks, and burst QPS (if known)
- Any hard latency SLOs (p95) or cost/latency tradeoffs you prefer

We’ll use these to model hosted vs. dedicated options and propose a pilot that optimizes for continuous batching where it makes sense. I attached a one‑pager pricing reference.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call week of Oct 19 to walk a modeled cost sheet. Let me know availability.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: volumes, $/1M target and batching assumptions

Alex — appreciate the clear list. High level answers below (these are internal estimates; procurement looped for budgeting):

- Monthly tokens: we expect 80M–150M tokens/month in year 1 if adoption follows our forecast.
- Target unit econ: our finance team is hoping to target ~$900 / 1M tokens (we're open to seeing tradeoffs at $700–$1,100).
- Budget band: initial pilot budget in the first 3 months is $30k–$80k; long-term commit TBD.
- Workload mix: ~70% chat (short back-and-forth), ~20% longer summaries (500–2,000 token jobs), ~10% embeddings (bulk nightly ingestion).
- Concurrency profile: baseline concurrent requests ~8–12; business-hour peaks ~50–80 concurrent sessions; rare bursts up to ~150 concurrent. Note: a lot of the traffic is low-latency interactive chat — p95 target ideally <= 400ms, but we can tolerate up to 700ms for background summary jobs.
- Latency/cost tradeoff: prefer preserving interactivity for chat. Willing to accept slightly increased token-unit cost if it guarantees p95 < 400ms for chat.

I attached our internal SLO summary for reference. Happy to review your modeled pricing and batching assumptions on a call.

—Mark
Mark D'Souza
Head of Product, Inicio Health
[Attachment: Inicio_SLOs.pdf (pdf)]

Immediate asks:

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T08:11:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Mark's numbers — batching window sensitivity & workload patterns

Quick modelling notes and assumptions (high-level) — I attached a working spreadsheet with the walkthrough.

Assumptions used to map tokens -> requests -> concurrency:
- Use cases: chat (70%), summaries (20%), embeddings (10%).
- Average tokens per request: chat = 120 tokens, summary = 1,200 tokens, embedding batch requests processed offline (per-job token count varies).
- For 100M tokens/month baseline (midpoint of Mark's range):
  * Requests/month (chat portion) ~ (100M * 0.7) / 120 ≈ 583k chat requests/month (rest are larger jobs)
  * That maps to ~6.7 requests/sec average (all-day). Peaks are driven by user concurrency and message rate per session — with 60–80 concurrent sessions you can see instantaneous QPS in the 20–80 range depending on session activity.

Continuous batching guidance (practical expectations):
- Micro-batch windows: 50ms captures small sibling arrivals; 150ms captures higher aggregation and typically gives the best tradeoff for interactive apps; 300ms can improve token-efficiency further but may start to impact p95 for chat.
- Empirical efficiencies to use for modeling (conservative): 50ms => ~7–10% token cost reduction; 150ms => ~18–22%; 300ms => ~25–32% (varies with traffic burstiness). I used 8/20/28 in the attached calc as Alex suggested.
- Latency: for short chat (120 tokens avg) and a 150ms batching window, we can generally meet p95 <= 400ms on modern GPU-backed endpoints if kernel and kv-cache are optimized; 300ms windows push risk for p95 on tight SLOs.

Recommendations for the Oct 19 presentation:
- Show three modeled scenarios (80M / 110M / 150M tokens) each with Hosted vs Dedicated cost lines and continuous-batching windows (50/150/300ms). Highlight the $/1M achieved for each scenario and which configuration meets p95 <= 400ms.
- Highlight where embeddings and summary jobs (longer generations) should be routed to different instance types or scheduled off-peak to avoid polluting chat batching efficiency.
- Pilot proposal: 8-week pilot using Hosted with a small Dedicated reserve if the customer commits >100M tokens/month; include an SLA exception window for initial tuning.

Files attached: batch_model_estimate.xlsx (costs + latency model). I annotated the cells with the conservative multipliers; happy to iterate.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
